answer: Biometric enrollment with epoch nullifiers caps each operator's reward allowance. Before agents can claim for mapping a knoll, identifying a violet or inspecting a trellis, their operator proves possession of a deduplicated credential. The verifier accepts one allowance per credential per epoch across all accounts. N allowances need N enrolled people, whom an attacker must recruit or pay. This depends on reliable deduplication and liveness checks; stolen or falsely issued credentials bypass the bound.
